question: What is the main focus of community-centred health care?

options.A: Eliminating traditional medicine practices from rural settlements
options.B: Shifting health services directly into the living environments of populations
options.C: Focusing exclusively on individual inpatient curative treatments
options.D: Expanding high-tech surgical units within tertiary medical centres

explanation: Community-centred care prioritizes bringing health promotion and disease prevention directly to where people live and work rather than waiting for them to visit distant hospitals. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h1)

question: Why is empowering local populations essential in community-centred practice?

options.A: It guarantees immediate eradication of all infectious diseases
options.B: It removes all financial responsibilities from the national government
options.C: It enables communities to take charge of their own health determinants
options.D: It completely replaces the need for trained professional nurses

explanation: Empowerment builds local capacity, ensuring sustainable health outcomes through active community participation and ownership. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h1)

question: Which international declaration formally defined Primary Health Care principles?
explanation: The Alma-Ata Declaration of 1978 established the core philosophy and foundational principles of Primary Health Care globally. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h2)

question: A community health nurse collaborates with the local agriculture extension worker to improve infant nutrition. What primary health care principle is demonstrated?
explanation: Working across different sectors like agriculture and health addresses the root social determinants of nutritional status. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h2)

question: What does comprehensive health care integrate into a single continuum?

options.A: Private insurance and commercial pharmacy operations
options.C: Surgical, pharmaceutical, and radiological specialties only
options.D: Preventive, promotive, curative, and rehabilitative services

explanation: Comprehensive health care covers the full spectrum of human health needs, from preventing illness to restoring function and rehabilitation. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h3)

question: A nurse treats a child for diarrhea and also inspects the family water source. Why is this comprehensive care?

options.A: It focuses exclusively on expensive laboratory diagnostic testing
options.B: It addresses both immediate illness and the underlying environmental cause
options.C: It fulfills mandatory hospital discharge documentation requirements
options.D: It eliminates the need for any pharmaceutical intervention

explanation: Comprehensive care looks beyond the acute episode of disease to examine and correct environmental and social determinants of health. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h3)

question: What is a windshield survey during a community health assessment?

options.A: Observing community life and environmental conditions while moving through the area
options.B: Testing drinking water samples inside a sterile microbiology laboratory
options.C: Reviewing past hospital admission registers from the regional medical records
options.D: Administering written questionnaires to every household head inside a clinic

explanation: A windshield survey is an observational method where the nurse assesses housing, sanitation, and community life firsthand. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h4)

question: Why is relying solely on clinic attendance records a flawed community assessment strategy?

options.A: It takes too much time for busy nursing personnel to compile
options.B: It violates patient confidentiality policies under health laws
options.C: It generates too much digital data for manual tally sheets
options.D: It misses vulnerable individuals who never reach formal health facilities

explanation: Clinic records suffer from selection bias because they exclude people facing geographical or financial barriers to care. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h4)

question: What does cultural competence in community nursing primarily require?

options.A: Replacing all traditional health beliefs with strict biomedical science
options.B: Refusing to communicate with traditional birth attendants
options.C: Respecting local beliefs while addressing harmful health practices
options.D: Adopting local tribal scarring traditions personally

explanation: Cultural competence bridges the gap between professional nursing standards and local beliefs without causing alienation. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h5)

question: Why should community nurses engage with traditional birth attendants?

options.A: To hand over complete clinical authority to untrained community members
options.B: To increase out-of-pocket expenses for pregnant village women
options.C: To avoid working inside government-approved primary health centres
options.D: To bridge the gap between local practices and safe institutional delivery

explanation: Engaging traditional birth attendants helps redirect high-risk pregnancies to health facilities and improves overall maternal safety. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h5)

question: What is a key indicator of sustainability in a community health program?

options.A: Constant replacement of local health volunteers by visiting researchers
options.B: Local community members taking over management of the health initiative
options.C: Permanent deployment of international medical doctors to village clinics
options.D: Continuous heavy reliance on foreign non-governmental organizations

explanation: Sustainability means a project continues to function effectively using local resources and leadership after external support ends. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h6)

question: How should a community nurse evaluate the success of an immunization campaign?

options.A: By counting the number of empty vaccine vials left in the clinic store
options.B: By checking if international agencies published the report in a journal
options.C: By measuring vaccine coverage rates alongside community involvement
options.D: By evaluating whether the local government increased taxes for health

explanation: Effective evaluation combines hard statistical coverage data with assessments of ongoing local participation and ownership. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h6)
